title: First music: homemade neighborhood bands
summary: His parents were not musical; neighborhood boys made wash-tub bass drums, cheese-box kettle drums and kazoos.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up a first guitar or banjo, self-taught

blocks.x: Well can you tell me about the first music you ever heard? Did your folks play, your parents play any instruments?

Well, no, neither of my parents was more or less musically inclined, I wouldn't think so. But we've got a bunch of fellas in the neighborhood have got the experiment from listening to various groups that used to participate in ones at the time. And we used to have what you call bands of our own, wherein one fella played the bass drum which was comprised of an old beat out wash tub. Then another fella would play the kettle drums which was, oh the kettle drum was made out of one of these old antique cheese boxes. I don't know whether you remember seeing those around.

And of course our biggest instrument, wind instrument at the time was what you call a kazoo. I don't know whether you've heard of the kazoo or not, but we had various forms of the kazoo. It was one form, we had it made like a trumpet, and another form it was made like a clarinet. We'd go through the motions and just play a whole lot of the old songs that we used to listen to.
One of our friends, Edward Johnson, they call him Noon, he's not knowing that it has a bazooka.
It has a slide. Oh yes, yes, yes.
